core.title: Size a wagon on two axes: footprint and separability
core.given: A wagon is being designed, sized or recomposed.
core.when: The planner decides the wagon's size and boundary.
core.then: Size the wagon on two orthogonal axes: SIZE (intrinsic footprint: how much work is inside) and SEPARABILITY (is the wagon a well-separated unit in the produce/consume graph, i.e. is the cut correct?), and treat complexity as super-linear in cross-wagon coupling, not additive in component count.
prefer: Size axis: the additive footprint, sum(count x weight), from the footprint-scoring convention (planner.feature.footprint-scoring).

Separability axis: a wagon is separable when its cohesion (shared-artifact / object-of-control density of its own WMBTs) is at least its tightest coupling (shared produce/consume artifact-name weight) to any single neighbor wagon.
avoid: Sizing a wagon on footprint alone.
Treating complexity as additive in component count.
core.why: Complexity is super-linear in cross-wagon coupling, so footprint alone cannot tell you whether a cut is correct.
evidence: Nonbinding illustration (the source is documentation-only; this is not an acceptance requirement): wagon sizing reasoning, where it exists, does not treat a small footprint as proof of a correct cut.
verification: Documentation-only disposition, severity 2: this rule has no detector of its own and imposes no acceptance evidence.

Terms for any future check: size_axis = intrinsic footprint, the additive volume of components (per the footprint-scoring convention, planner.feature.footprint-scoring). separability_axis = coupling complexity, i.e. whether the wagon is a well-separated unit in the produce/consume graph. cohesion = intra-wagon shared-artifact / object-of-control density of a wagon's own WMBTs. coupling = shared produce/consume artifact-name weight between a wagon and a neighbor wagon. separable = internal cohesion is at least the tightest coupling to any single neighbor.

fires: The planner designs or sizes a new wagon.
The planner sizes a wagon and has considered only its footprint.
doesNotFire: Pure footprint scoring of a feature where no wagon boundary is being decided (the footprint-scoring convention, planner.feature.footprint-scoring, alone applies).
Code edits inside a wagon that change neither its WMBTs, its boundary, nor its produce/consume declarations.

neutralityNotes: This rule is a planning-methodology principle with no stack mechanics: it names no runtime, framework, language, package manager, file suffix or path, so bunOnly is empty. 'Wagon', 'WMBT' and 'produce/consume' are framework planning-model concepts already carried by the neutral vocabulary (layout.wagon_dir, urn.wmbt, roles.plan_artifact.kinds), so they remain in the core. The sibling reference planner.feature.footprint-scoring is kept by id; a stack realization should resolve it to that sibling rule's current id in the same ruleset. activation.facts[2] is the only profile-dependent item: the core fires on the neutral file kind 'plan artifact', instantiated per stack by roles.plan_artifact.kinds. The per-fact 'note' strings of bun.json (auxiliary commentary, not item content) are not carried into the core's activation facts, whose schema has no note field.
